questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used.

Eyepiece graticules and stage micrometers are used to measure cells. Which is the correct reason why an eyepiece graticule is calibrated?

options.A: An eyepiece graticule can be used to make measurements.
options.B: An eyepiece graticule is magnified by the objective lens.
options.C: An eyepiece graticule magnifies the specimen.

options.A: W only B X only C W and X only D W, X and Y

A naturally occurring polysaccharide is a branched chain of α-glucose. The straight parts of the molecule are linked by α-1, 6 glycosidic bonds with a small number of branches which are linked by either an α-1, 3 glycosidic bond or an α-1, 4 glycosidic bond. Which polysaccharide has a structure most similar to that described?
Which molecule has properties that are not dependent on hydrogen bonds?
What occurs during protein denaturation by extremes of pH?
When the ice on the surface of a pond melts, which changes benefit the ecosystem in the pond?
How does increasing substrate concentration affect the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction in the presence of a competitive inhibitor?

options.A: The rate of the reaction decreases.
options.B: The rate of the reaction decreases initially and then recovers.
options.C: The rate of the reaction increases.
options.D: The rate of the reaction is not affected.

questions.questionText: Four students investigated the effect of catalase on hydrogen peroxide. Each student started a digital clock at the beginning of the experiment and stopped the clock after

bubbles had been counted. The time recorded on the digital clock is shown below. hours minutes seconds hundredths 00 01 33 54 Which student recorded the results to the best level of precision for the apparatus used? student time recorded
Which of the following can decrease the fluidity of the cell surface membrane?
Which process would allow the movement of large protein molecules out of the cell?

Strips of potato tissue were immersed in distilled water or in sucrose solutions of different concentrations. The graph shows the percentage change in length of the potato tissue over time. distilled water _
Uncontrolled cell division of cancer cells forms tumours. Which statement describes the difference between a cancer cell and a normal cell?

options.A: Cancer cells do not undergo cytokinesis.
options.B: Cancer cells do not have metaphase.
options.C: Cancer cells have a shorter interphase.
options.D: Only cancer cells have mutated DNA.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a cell nucleus in prophase of mitosis. Which statement describes the chromosomes found in each daughter nucleus immediately following division of this cell by mitosis?

options.C: 8 chromosomes, each containing 1 molecule of DNA
options.D: 4 chromosomes, each containing 1 molecule of DNA

questions.questionText: Gene mutations in either the BRCA1 or the BRCA2 genes are responsible for the majority of hereditary breast cancer in humans. The proteins produced by the two genes migrate to the nucleus where they interact with other proteins, such as those produced by the tumour suppressor gene, p53 and the DNA repair gene, RAD51. Which combination of gene activity is most likely to result in breast cancer? gene BRCA1 or p53 RAD51 BRCA2
One gene provides the code for the production of which molecule?

A polypeptide has the amino acid sequence glycine – arginine – lysine – serine. The table gives possible tRNA anticodons for each amino acid. amino acid tRNA anticodons arginine UCC GCG glycine CCA CCU lysine UUC UUU serine AGG UCG Which sequence of bases on DNA would code for the polypeptide?
What is the minimum number of hydrogen bonds in a length of DNA containing 700 nucleotides?
The diagram shows a xerophytic leaf in different conditions, P and Q. X X P Q Which statements describe the difference between the cells in layer X in conditions P and Q?
A potometer can be used to measure transpiration rates in a plant. Why is the plant stem cut under water before attaching to the potometer?

options.A: to maintain the turgidity of the xylem vessels
options.B: to prevent collapse of the xylem vessels
options.C: to stop air entering the xylem vessels
options.D: to stop water loss from the xylem vessels

Humans have a double circulation system. What does the term ‘double circulation’ mean?

options.A: The blood circulates separately in the two sides of the heart.
options.B: The blood passes twice through the heart during one complete circulation.
options.C: The heart has two of each chamber; atria and ventricles.
options.D: The heart beat has a double sound caused by the two sets of valves closing.

questions.questionText: The photomicrograph shows a section through part of a bronchus wall. X What is the function of the tissue labelled X?

options.B: helps to widen the airway after an allergic reaction
options.C: produces mucus to trap dust particles and bacteria
options.D: supports the airway to prevent collapse

questions.questionText: Why is the inner lining of the bronchiole folded?

options.A: to allow for expansion during breathing

questions.questionText: Some antibiotics are used in animal feed to reduce disease. What explains why these antibiotics should not be used in the treatment of human diseases?

options.A: Humans may be allergic to these antibiotics.
options.B: Human cells may stop responding to these antibiotics.
options.C: Pathogenic bacteria may develop resistance to these antibiotics.
options.D: Useful gut bacteria may be killed by these antibiotics.

questions.questionText: Which statement about both B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes is correct?

options.A: They become active only when a specific antibody binds to their surface receptor.
options.B: They divide to form clones when meeting an antitoxin in a cell.
options.C: They produce memory cells to respond to an antigen when exposed in the future.
options.D: They release hormone-like cytokines which stimulate release of antibodies.
